utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, and happy new year to everyone, regardless of where they are in the calender. I realise, Mr. Bezbradica, that you still have some time to go before you reach new year, according to your calender. But nevertheless, happy new year. Could we have the case called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-79-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the representation. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Anna Richterova and Karen Beausey for the Prosecution, together with Willem Wijermars, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Stevo Bezbradica, counsel for the accused, Mico Stanisic, and our legal consultant, Mr. Slobodan Cvijetic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's fair to say that the case has now reached a state where we could look with some confidence into the trial phase, and I would like to start out by disclosing what I know as to the matters at hand when it come to scheduling. I think within a time period which is not going to be specified, but could happen this or possibly beginning of next month, this case will be transferred to a Trial Chamber, and that means that this case, if we look at scheduling, would probably be scheduled to commence somewhere between Easter and before the summer recess. It's difficult to pinpoint a time. As parties are aware and I have said so on previous occasions, the matter of scheduling is in the hand of overriding interests, and cases could change when they are slotted for and docketed but I think it's safe to say now that this case has now matured to such a state that it is pretty much on the top of the list. I know, Mr. Bezbradica, that you have requested a three-month notice and you consider yourself to be put on notice by this, which we have now imparted in the courtroom. With those introductory remarks, I would like to make sure that we have the same understanding as to issues that are outstanding. And let me say, these outstanding issues, which are motions pending, some of them will probably be taken in by the new Trial Chamber and others will be taken in the composition which we have at the moment. And as I said, I am not ready to - no one is - to say when this transfer will be effected. The motions that I have on my list, and that is the same list that was discussed with the senior legal officer yesterday at the 65 ter conference, is a motion for protective measures from the Prosecution, filed confidentially on the 28th of February, 2007. And we have an old motion from the Defence regarding Prosecution's noncompliance with Rule 65 ter (E) and a corrigendum on both of those are from the 16th of March and 8th of May respectively. And then we have a motion from the Prosecution for leave to amend the revised amended indictment which was filed on the 9th of May, last year. We have two Defence motions dealing with the question of the rescinding or varying the delayed disclosures in two cases, one in the Brdjanin case and one in the Krajisnik case. And finally on the back of the decision which was issued by the Chamber on the 14th of December last year on adjudicated facts, there is a request by the Defence for certification to appeal that decision, a request which the Prosecution responded to on the 7th of January this year. Those are my record, the outstanding motions that we have to deal with. Does that meet with the parties' understanding as well? Ms. Richterova?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, we are not aware of any other outstanding motions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, everything is correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. If we then leave that for a moment aside and look ahead, there is, since now the work plan has for all practical purposes been complied with and followed, I would like to put a matter for consideration primarily by the Prosecution to add to this, and that is the question of when 92 bis, ter, quater and also the expert report on the 94 bis should be filed, and I understand the matter was discussed yesterday. And is it possible to have an indication, Mrs. Richterova, when you would be prepared, from the Prosecution side, to have these filings in?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: As we discussed yesterday, we would be ready to file it by the end of February. Of course, we are fully in your hands. We are talking about motions pursuant to Rule 92 bis, 92 ter and 94. The reason why we are asking for this time is that based on the Trial Chamber's decision regarding the adjudicated facts, we now have to review all our witness statements. Also, as we discussed yesterday, this decision will have impact, significant in fact, on presentation of our case regarding eight municipalities, and because we would really like to streamline the case, our intention is to present evidence, as far as possible, as much as possible, in the written form, and therefore we have to re-evaluate all of our witnesses and also re-evaluate our 65 ter list of witnesses. So this is the reason why we are asking for the end of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. May I clarify so I understand this. I understand, obviously, the importance and the impact of the 14th of December decision, but am I right in assuming that you, regardless of this, also are assessing your witness list?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Of course. Of course, we are, and we have been working on assessment of our witnesses, and not only witnesses, of course, we are reviewing again the number of our exhibits. And as we mentioned yesterday, we intend to seek leave to amend both our 65 ter list of witnesses and list of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Richterova. Well, I fully understand the work that you are addressing and the need for you to have sufficient time to do that, and I'm not opposed to the suggestion of giving you a time limit until the end of February this year, meaning that the 29th of February, 2008, is a time by which you should file 92 bis, 92 ter and 94 bis reports and statements. I understand from it that 92 quater is not on your mind at the moment, but should you change your mind, that would be the time also for that type of statement to be filed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And, in fact, I omitted 92 quater. Yes, we will file also a motion regarding Rule 92 quater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So with that decision, the work plan has now been amended accordingly. I also understand that when it comes to matters of disclosure, parties, at earlier status conferences, had discussions on this, but this seems to now be progressing with the meeting of minds of the parties, and of course the Prosecution has the ongoing obligation to disclose under Rule 68. Do you have anything to comment on disclosure, Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: No, I don't have, Your Honour, only I can confirm that regarding disclosure, at the moment everything is in order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, with the noting of outstanding motions, the addition to set a new timetable regarding 92 bis and related statements and 94 bis, I do not have any other matters that I would like to raise with the parties, apart from the following: I'm aware that the issue of the decision of the 14th of December, in the sense that that is not final, i.e., the Chamber is now considering the motion from the Defence and the response from the Prosecution on the question of certification of appeal, and that is obviously an uncertainty that we will seek to have clarified as soon as is practically possible, but given that uncertainty, I would certainly not at this point discourage the parties to seek to engage in further discussions on the matters of agreed facts and related matters. I understood from the conference yesterday that there were discussions ongoing on the matters of agreed facts, some related to the decision and some unrelated to it, and maybe I think it's proper also to have that discussion on the record, so I turn to you first, Mrs. Richterova, whether you would like to impart something on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: There have been ongoing discussion regarding agreed facts, unfortunately not very successful. Your Honour will remember that during our last status conference, we discussed the Prosecution proposal of approximately 60 agreed facts. The Defence counsel replied that his client object to all but 26 and that they would provide us with explanation why the other facts are not suitable as agreed facts, and at the same time they also offered that they would try to re-formulate or suggest some changes. Unfortunately, it hasn't happened. What we have done is, based on the Trial Chamber's decision and at least based on these 26 agreed facts, we put together a list of facts to which both parties at various stages agreed, and it was the only purpose, the only rationale behind this list, so that we have one consolidated list of agreed facts which are comprised of adjudicated facts proposed by the Prosecution and agreed facts proposed -- adjudicated facts proposed by the Defence, and really agreed facts between parties. We sent a letter to Mr. Bezbradica to review this list, and the purpose was for him to review to check whether there are any typos, any errors, and unfortunately we haven't heard anything from the Defence counsel until now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Richterova. And what do you have to say to this, Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the situation is a little bit different than the Prosecution now -- in her allegation. We give our response to the Prosecution the 29th of November, 2007. I am instructed that way, and we are not going more further in much more details. And I don't know -- also, in that letter we already explained our proposal in some -- to the proposed facts, and I don't know what we can do more than we've done in such way. In regarding of submitted letters of Monday of this week, I received that letter -- I find that letter, as I said yesterday, on Monday afternoon. I was flying from Belgrade to The Hague. It wasn't possible to check everything. The Prosecution asked us to provide them with our final position regarding that letter. I'm not going to tell the Prosecution that we are not going to agree. There is already agreed -- we have agreed facts and adjudicated facts and everything is clear, but there is -- the letter does not include the same issue. The story is a little bit different, because they put some facts which are not considered as agreed facts. And because of that, already mailed that letter to my client, and at this stage I'm waiting for his instruction. I can't give final approval until -- until I have with him further discussion about that. And I will provide them with our response shortly. There is no doubt about that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bezbradica. Well, there may be some misunderstanding as to the nature of different types of facts, as can be seen from the decision handed down on the 14th of December. The Chamber considered that facts moved by the Prosecution or, for that matter, from the other side, as adjudicated facts and not opposed, as can be seen and noted down as agreed facts, and then of course we would have a set of other facts which are unrelated to the motions and the decision on the 14th of December, and I think it's obviously helpful if there at least could be a common understanding between the Defence and the Prosecution what you are talking about, and from the Chamber's side we can obviously only encourage the parties to come to and maximize the understanding. I fully -- Mr. Bezbradica, I realise that you are bound to follow instructions from your client. That is your duty as a Defence counsel. But you also have a duty to offer your professional assessment of the case and give him a sound basis for his instructions to you. I mean, the relationship between a principal and adviser is not a one-sided one, and I'm certainly not, Mr. Bezbradica, going to tell you how to perform your job, but I think it's important to remind ourselves that the Defence counsel is best serving his principal by offering him his assessment. He may not like it, but that is the duty of a Defence counsel to do so, because the duty of the Defence counsel is to see to the interests of the accused and not, for instance, to some other interests unrelated to the matter. And that brings me to a question which has been lingering for this case from time to time, namely, that the parties should be encouraged not only to discuss matters of agreed facts and related matters but also to see whether the discussion could be broadened and maybe entail a change of position totally and change of plea on the case of the accused. And I understand that this summer there were some discussions, and I understand that there also was a meeting between the Prosecution and the accused. Am I correct on this, Mrs. Richterova?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and of course there was -- in September we also sent another letter to Mr. Bezbradica and his client, and of course the position is that there won't be any plea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bezbradica, is that the understanding that you have as well? Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the situation is a little bit different. It's correct that we have discussion in June/July last year and we put something in writing for the Prosecution, but I can't go further without my client. It's not really -- it is a big issue. And they never respond to our letter. We put something there, but I never received their respond. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, again, this may be a matter of misplaced communication or misunderstandings, but I will at this point only encourage, obviously, both sides, but especially you, Mr. Bezbradica, to -- even if it is a big issue, I'm certainly aware of that, but as things develop and the case matures, a Defence would be in a better position to assess whatever proposition is put to them from the Prosecution. I'm not encouraging you to give up any of your right or change your position as far as your present interests of the accused dictate, but I certainly would encourage you to approach the matter with maybe more vigour than so far has been the case. And again I'm not privy and I don't want to be privy with discussions which you have with your client, but I reinforce that the duty of a Defence counsel is one of also putting the matters to the accused in such a way that he is available to make an informed decision. And I'm certain, Mr. Bezbradica, that you have done so. I just want to have this said in order to avoid any misunderstanding on it, and I'm certain that at this stage nothing is too late. If there is a dialogue on the questions of agreed facts that could be broadened into other issues, I'm certain it's never too late for the parties to have a new position on old issues, as it were. So this is -- I bring this up because -- to take away the perception that just because a case has reached a state where it has matured to be taken to trial, these discussions which have been ongoing should not cease. On the contrary, I think it would be opportune to try to reinforce that, and I'm certain, Mr. Bezbradica, that you will convey to your client the position now as stated. I had not thought to raise any other matter, and just before we adjourn I'd like to hear whether the parties do have anything else that they would like to raise at this status conference. Mrs. Richterova?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour, we have no other matters to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Bezbradica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we don't have anything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, with that, we now stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
